significance: A 13th-century Shiva temple whose inscriptions credit Parakrama Pandyan I, best known as one of the 27 Nakshatra temples of Tamil Nadu, linked to the Pushya asterism and holding a Shani shrine with his consorts Jyestha and Mandha.
story: The legend here has Shani, lamed by Yama, tripping over the roots of a vila tree at this spot on Akshaya Tritiya, whereupon Shiva appeared as Akshayapureeswarar, healed him and blessed him with marriage.
